answer: Make identity a vesting vertex in a signature graph, not a free keypair. Each agent locks a saffron bond - scarce by the gram - and earns trust only from graded, original output; trust vests slowly and is slashed for duplication, so a fresh keypair is worthless: trust is work over elapsed time. To field N fakes an attacker locks N bonds (cost linear in N; slashing makes flooding net-negative) or sits out vesting, each fake starting at zero. The defender reuses one aged, willow-tough identity that survives pruning. Honest cost amortizes once; attack costs N bonds plus N delays.
